title_ar: الشيخ الددو: التصويت بـ"نعم" على دستور مصر واجب شرعي
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew: Voting 'Yes' on Egypt's Constitution Is Obligatory in the Sharia
body_ar:
قال الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء بموريتانيا إن التصويت بـ"نعم" على دستور مصر الجديد الذي سيتم الاستفتاء عليه يوم غد السبت 15 ديسمبر 2012 فريضة شرعية على كل مصري، معتبرا أن ذلك يصد المؤامرة التي تحاك ضد مصر، وهو من نصرة الحق.

وأضاف الشيخ الذي كان يتحدث اليوم الجمعة 14 ديسمبر 2012 في تلفزيون قطر ضمن برنامج "حياة القلوب" تحت عنوان "نهضة الأمة" أن أمر المصريين لن يستقيم إلا باتفاقهم على دستورهم، وأن السعي إلى إقراره سيؤدي إلى كف الضرر وتحقيق المصلحة.

وانتقد الشيخ التصرفات التي يقوم بها المناوئون للدستور وللنظام المصري الحالي، معتبرا أنهم هم من كان يدعم النظام السابق ويؤيده في كل قراراته، داعيا الرئيبس المصري محمد مرسي إلى أن يتجه إلى تحقيق الحق والعدل وتوفير الأمن والرخاء بين مختلف التوجهات، بما في ذلك احتواء الفلول وإشراكهم فيما يتيسر وفيما يقبلون.

وأوضح الشيخ الددو أن الله سبحانه وتعالى ائتمن الرئيس مرسي على مصر وعلى شعبها ومواردها...وأن الأمة تؤمل فيه الخير الكثير..وعليه أن يستمر في نهجه ولا يلين للضغوط بما في ذلك الضغوطات الدولية، مشيرا إلى أنه على الثوار المصريين أن يعلموا أن النظام الذي ثاروا عليه يتكون من ثلاث سلط: تشريعية وتنفيذية وقضائية وعليهم تطهيرها الثلاثة..فلابد للقضاء أن يتخلص من الفلول أيضا..

وشبه الشيخ الددو النظام المصري السابق وفلوله بقصة فرعون التي تتكون فيها منظومة الدولة من خمسة أركان: الملك و يمثله فرعون، و.الوزير المنافق ويمثله هامان، و رجل الأعمال والمال المناصر ويمثله قارون، و رجل الدين الذي يسخر علمه لخدمة الطغيان، ويمثله السحرة، و رجال الإعلام الذين يقلبون الحقائق، ويمثلهم الحاشرون..

وعرج الشيخ الددو على بعض القضايا الإسلامية الراهنة متحدثا عن مأساة الشعب البوري وما لاقاه من أذى وتنكيل وتشريد، وعن نضال الشعب السوري ووجوب نصرته، مضيفا أنه لابد من التعبير عن مقتضى الولاء والبراء، ومن لم يشعر بمأساة أمته ولم يساعدها ويتعاطف معها فلا خير فيه، داعيا أهل الخير ورجال الأعمال والؤسسات إلى أن تبادر إلى نصرة المسلمين.
body_en:
Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars in Mauritania, said that voting 'yes' on Egypt's new constitution, which is to be put to referendum tomorrow, Saturday 15 December 2012, is an obligation of the Sharia (farīḍah sharʿiyyah) upon every Egyptian, holding that this repels the conspiracy being woven against Egypt, and that it is part of supporting the truth.

The Sheikh, who was speaking today, Friday 14 December 2012, on Qatar Television within the programme 'The Life of Hearts', under the heading 'The Renaissance of the Community', added that the affairs of the Egyptians will not be set right except by their agreeing upon their constitution, and that striving for its approval will lead to the warding off of harm (mafsadah) and the achieving of benefit (maṣlaḥah).

The Sheikh criticised the conduct of those opposed to the constitution and to the present Egyptian regime, holding that they are the very ones who used to support the former regime and back it in all its decisions; and he called upon the Egyptian president Muhammad Morsi to set himself to realising truth and justice and to providing security and prosperity across the various orientations, including containing the remnants of the old regime (al-fulūl) and involving them in what is feasible and in what they will accept.

Sheikh al-Dedew explained that God, glorified and exalted, has entrusted President Morsi with Egypt, with its people and with its resources… and that the community hopes for much good from him… and that he must continue on his course and not soften towards pressures, including international pressures. He pointed out that the Egyptian revolutionaries must know that the regime against which they rose consists of three powers: legislative, executive and judicial, and that they must purge all three… for the judiciary too must rid itself of the remnants of the old regime…

Sheikh al-Dedew likened the former Egyptian regime and its remnants to the story of Pharaoh, in which the apparatus of the state consists of five pillars: the king, represented by Pharaoh; the hypocritical minister, represented by Haman; the supportive businessman and financier, represented by Qarun; the religious man who puts his learning at the service of tyranny, represented by the magicians; and the media men who invert the facts, represented by the gatherers.

Sheikh al-Dedew touched on some current Islamic issues, speaking of the tragedy of the Burmese people and the harm, persecution and displacement they have met with, and of the struggle of the Syrian people and the obligation to support them, adding that it is necessary to give expression to what loyalty and disavowal (al-walāʾ wa-l-barāʾ) requires, and that there is no good in one who does not feel his community's tragedy and does not help it and sympathise with it; and he called upon the people of good, upon businessmen and upon institutions to take the initiative in supporting the Muslims.

flags.context: التصويت بـ"نعم" على دستور مصر الجديد … فريضة شرعية على كل مصري
options: an obligation of the Sharia (farīḍah sharʿiyyah) upon every Egyptian
individually obligatory (farḍ ʿayn) upon every Egyptian
a religious duty upon every Egyptian
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW. A ruling of obligation attached to a named vote in a named referendum in a foreign state, reported at second hand from a television appearance. 'فريضة' is rendered on the fixed mapping as an obligation, with the Arabic carried. Option 1 would read the phrase as the technical farḍ ʿayn; the source does not say 'عين', so that reading is not adopted. Publication in English of the Sheikh ruling on a specific Egyptian ballot carries political and reputational exposure and is a decision for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: متحدثا عن مأساة الشعب البوري وما لاقاه من أذى وتنكيل وتشريد
options: the Burmese people (reading البوري as a misprint for البورمي)
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11). 'البوري' is not an ethnonym; in December 2012 the Sheikh was speaking of the Rohingya of Burma, and 'البورمي' is the evident reading. Translated by the evident sense and flagged rather than silently corrected; 'body_ar' preserves the source spelling.

options: the remnants of the old regime (al-fulūl)
the leftovers of the former regime
flags.note: Egyptian political term of art of the 2011–13 period for holdovers of the Mubarak regime. It is pejorative in Arabic; the English keeps the Arabic alongside so the reader sees it is a partisan label and not a neutral description.

flags.context: وأن السعي إلى إقراره سيؤدي إلى كف الضرر وتحقيق المصلحة
options: the warding off of harm (mafsadah) and the achieving of benefit (maṣlaḥah)
the prevention of damage and the securing of interest
flags.note: The source has 'الضرر', not 'المفسدة'. The glossary rendering of mafsadah is used because the pairing with maṣlaḥah here is clearly the technical one, but a reviewer may prefer to keep 'harm (ḍarar)' to stay closer to the wording used.

translator_notes: News report of a television appearance, not a written fatwā. Marked critical_for_display because the headline presents a ruling on a specific 2012 Egyptian ballot as the Sheikh's standing position; read in English fourteen years later and out of its moment it will be taken for a general rule about voting. Source typos preserved in body_ar: 'الرئيبس' for 'الرئيس', 'والؤسسات' for 'والمؤسسات', 'البوري' for 'البورمي'. 'الحاشرون' alludes to the summoners Pharaoh sent out in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:36–53, and is rendered plainly as 'the gatherers'. CMS date is a bulk-upload timestamp, not a composition date.
